doc.title: Norman Simmons interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 27, 2007 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Opening and coming up in Chicago
title: Growing up poor but not feeling poor
summary: Everyone was on the same level, things were cheaper, and community was different.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you think, or did your father think of your family as poor?
No. And you talk to a lot of people in those days and they’ll say they didn’t know they were poor. They didn’t think about being poor. Because everybody was kind of on the

same level. So there wasn’t a lot — and thing were a lot cheaper. We didn’t have that kind of a capitalism them. And we were more of a democracy then than we are today, so we didn’t have people intentionally just stepping over people trying to get ahead. So it was a different kind of community in general then.
